issue_context.title: Job tests: use testing loggers
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Use `NewLogger` or `NewTestContext` from `k8s.io/klog/ktesting` in `pkg/controller/job` and `test/integration/job`.

/sig apps

### Why is this needed?

In most tests, we are using `context.Background()`. Using a testing logger allows us to associate the controller logs to a specific test, and only see them in the output if the test fails.

review_comments: oh cool, it looks like we didn't need the wrapping in this one :)
I wonder if this test is leaking routines. We are not canceling the parent context, which is used for `go.manager.Run`
I've added a t.Cleanup when the context is created
oh, here we actually need `context.Background()` or just a new context, because we are calling this after calling `cancel`.

nit: Why is this test we call `NewTestContext` at both levels: the test and individual test cases? I looked at other tests and it seems we are generally creating the context either for the whole test or per test case, but we don't seem consistent: `TestSyncJobWithJobBackoffLimitPerIndex` is per test, while `TestSyncJobWithJobSuccessPolicy` is per test case.

It looks like we need both, because there is code at both levels that need a context. And, in general, we want to associate any logs produced for a subtest to the subtest, not the parent test.

However, it looks odd that we are just overriding the context instead of creating a child of it.

Perhaps we need support from `ktesting` to do this better. Something like `log, ctx := ktesting.WithT(ctx, t)`.

@pohly do you have any other suggestion?

I think it's okay to call `ktesting.NewTestContext` multiple times at different levels. There's nothing in the context of the parent context that the sub-test needs to inherit, is it? `ktesting.NewTestContext` itself puts a logger for `t` there which would just get overridden by a second call.

> There's nothing in the context of the parent context that the sub-test needs to inherit, is it?

Not in this or other tests in this change, I think. But, it seems safer to inherit the context, specially if the parent context is canceled.

But we can leave it for a follow up.
